members.name: persuasion_v4a
members.instructions: This is a chat in which a persuader tries to get the persuadee to donate their task payment to the charity Save the Children. Which persuasion strategy or dialogue act does the final 'Persuader message to tag' use? Classify only that message; use the earlier dialogue as context (e.g. to tell whether it answers a question or agrees with a statement).

criteria.greeting_hello: Opening greeting: 'Hi!', 'Hello there', 'Hey, nice to meet you'.
criteria.greeting_how_are_you: Asks how the persuadee is, or replies to the persuadee's how-are-you, however short ('How are you today?', 'I'm good, how about you?', 'I am doing well thank you', 'Doing ok here.', 'Pretty good, enjoying the weather').
criteria.thank: Thanks the persuadee ('Thank you so much', 'Thanks for your donation', 'I appreciate it').
criteria.praise_user: Compliments or praises the persuadee or their decision ('That's awesome and generous!', 'People like you make the world better', 'You are a kind person', a bare 'Great!' right after they agree to donate).
criteria.acknowledge_agree: Responds to a statement the persuadee just made by agreeing, empathising with it or showing understanding: 'Me too.', 'Absolutely.', 'That is true', 'Yes, they are.', 'I understand that', 'That horrifies me!', 'I know what you mean'.
criteria.closing: Goodbye or closing remark ('Have a great night!', 'I hope you enjoy the rest of your day', 'Nice chatting with you').
criteria.answer_or_filler: A bare 'Yes'/'No' answering a persuadee question, a flat filler not replying to a how-are-you ('Ok...', 'yeah', 'yes, indeed'), a fragment, or a reply about the persuader's own situation that is not an argument.
criteria.sympathy_for_user: Sympathy for the persuadee's own hardship ('I'm so sorry to hear that', 'I understand financial strain').
criteria.small_talk: Small talk unrelated to the charity or donating, such as where people live or travel, or comments about the survey/HIT itself.
criteria.off_task: Completely off-topic message clearly unrelated to the conversation, the charity or the task.
criteria.credibility_org_info: Describes, introduces or praises Save the Children itself: naming or introducing the charity, what it is and what it does, where it works, its history and founder, its programs, ratings, awards, celebrity supporters, how funds are used, its website or URL, or that the charity is tackling a problem.
criteria.logical_reasoning: Reasons why one should donate or how a donation has an effect: 'Your donation could help many children', 'They can only help when people donate', moral reasoning ('we should all pitch in', 'everyone deserves a chance'), cost comparisons ('the cost of a coffee').
criteria.emotion_suffering: Tries to make the persuadee feel something: sad facts or statistics about children suffering or dying, any vivid mention of children who are hungry, killed, in war zones or without basic needs (even when the sentence also says a donation helps them), a story about a particular child, guilt ('you're just selfish'), the persuader expressing sadness or heartbreak about the children's situation, heartfelt pleas that children need help and are our future.
criteria.foot_in_the_door: Asks for or stresses a small amount as a first step: 'Every little bit helps', 'Even a small amount makes a difference', 'Any amount is welcome', 'just a few cents'.
criteria.self_modeling: The persuader says they themselves donate or will donate, to set an example: 'I will donate too', 'I'll match your donation', 'I gave what was given to me', 'I usually donate to this cause'.
criteria.personal_story: The persuader tells an anecdote from their own life or experience, e.g. work abroad, seeing poverty first-hand, a family member who was helped.
criteria.donation_info: Procedural information about how the donation works: it is deducted from the task payment, the allowed range ($0 to $2), the research team collects and sends it, how to donate.
criteria.propose_donation: Asks or urges the persuadee to donate, without asking for an amount: 'Would you be willing to donate some of your payment?', 'Would you consider donating?', 'Donate some money maybe?', 'You can do that right now.'
criteria.ask_amount: A question asking the persuadee how much they will donate: 'How much would you like to give?', 'What amount would you feel comfortable donating?', 'Half of 1 dollar?'. Statements that merely mention or suggest an amount are not this.
criteria.suggest_amount: A statement urging or suggesting that the persuadee donate, possibly naming an amount: 'We usually suggest a monthly donation of $5', 'May I suggest $.50?', '$2 you won't miss.'
criteria.amount_info: Information about what donation amounts are possible or what they buy in general, not addressed as a request: 'You can choose any amount from $0 to $2', 'supporting a child by $1 a day or $30 a month'.
criteria.source_inquiry: Asks whether the persuadee has heard of or knows about Save the Children or the organization.
criteria.task_inquiry: Asks the persuadee about donating, charities or the cause: 'Do you donate to charities?', 'Is this something you care about?', 'Have you heard of children separated at the border?', 'Have you ever seen the rate of illiteracy?', 'Is there any information I could provide?'. Includes questions asking whether the persuadee knows about or has seen a problem, when no statistic is stated.
criteria.personal_inquiry: Asks about the persuadee's personal life: 'Do you have children?', 'Where are you from?', 'What do you do for work?'.

members.name: persuasion_v4b
members.instructions: In this chat a persuader is trying to convince a crowd worker to give some of their task payment to Save the Children. Look only at the last line, the 'Persuader message to tag', and pick the persuasion strategy or dialogue act it performs. The earlier lines are context, for example to see whether it replies to a question or agrees with something the persuadee said.

criteria.greeting_hello: A hello that opens the chat, e.g. 'Hey there!', 'Hi', 'Hello, nice to meet you'.
criteria.greeting_how_are_you: A how-are-you question, or any reply to the persuadee asking how the persuader is, even a brief one: 'How's your day?', 'Good, and you?', 'Doing ok here.', 'I'm well, thanks', 'Pretty good, enjoying the weather'.
criteria.thank: Expresses gratitude to the persuadee: 'Thanks so much', 'Thank you for donating', 'I appreciate your time'.
criteria.praise_user: Says something nice about the persuadee or their choice: 'You're so generous!', 'People like you make a difference', 'What a kind thing to do', a bare 'Awesome!' when they have just agreed to give.
criteria.acknowledge_agree: Reacts to what the persuadee just said by agreeing, relating or showing understanding: 'I agree', 'Me too.', 'Absolutely.', 'That's true', 'I definitely understand.', 'I know what you mean', 'Wow, that's terrible!'.
criteria.closing: Ends the conversation or says goodbye: 'Have a good night!', 'Enjoy your day', 'Nice talking to you'.
criteria.answer_or_filler: A plain yes/no reply to the persuadee's question, an empty filler that is not a reply to a how-are-you ('Ok...', 'yeah', 'yes, indeed'), a sentence fragment, or the persuader talking about themselves without making an argument.
criteria.sympathy_for_user: Commiserates with a difficulty in the persuadee's own life: 'Sorry to hear that', 'I know money is tight for many people'.
criteria.small_talk: Chit-chat that has nothing to do with the charity or giving, such as hometowns, travel, the weather, or remarks about the HIT/survey.
criteria.off_task: A message wholly unrelated to the chat, the charity and the task.
criteria.credibility_org_info: Tells the persuadee about Save the Children: introduces or names it, explains what it is and does, its programs, the countries it works in, its history or founder, its reputation, ratings, awards, famous supporters, how it spends money, its website/URL, or that it is working on a problem.
criteria.logical_reasoning: Gives a reason to donate or explains the effect a donation has: 'Your gift could help many kids', 'They rely on donations to do their work', moral arguments ('we should all chip in', 'everyone deserves a fair chance'), price comparisons ('less than a cup of coffee').
criteria.emotion_suffering: Appeals to feelings: sad facts or figures about children who suffer or die, vivid mention of kids who are starving, killed, in war zones or lacking basics (even if the sentence also says a donation helps), a story about one child, guilt-tripping ('you just don't care'), the persuader saying how sad or heartbroken they are, heartfelt pleas that the children need help and are our future.
criteria.foot_in_the_door: Emphasises that a small gift is enough as a first step: 'Every bit counts', 'Even a little makes a difference', 'Just a few cents would help'.
criteria.self_modeling: The persuader states that they give or will give themselves, as an example: 'I'm donating too', 'I'll match whatever you give', 'I donated my payment', 'I give to this cause every year'.
criteria.personal_story: The persuader recounts something that happened in their own life: working abroad, seeing poverty up close, a relative who was helped.
criteria.donation_info: Explains the mechanics of the donation: it comes out of the task payment, the researchers collect it and pass it to the charity, how and where to give, that any amount is acceptable.
criteria.propose_donation: Asks or encourages the persuadee to give, without asking how much: 'Would you donate part of your payment?', 'Could you consider a donation?', 'Maybe donate a little?', 'You can do it right now.'
criteria.ask_amount: A question about how much the persuadee will give: 'How much would you like to donate?', 'What amount are you comfortable with?', 'Half of a dollar?'. Not statements that only mention or recommend an amount.
criteria.suggest_amount: A statement recommending that the persuadee give, often with a figure: 'We usually suggest $5 a month', 'Maybe $.50?', '$2 you won't miss.'
criteria.amount_info: General facts about possible amounts or what an amount pays for, not phrased as a request: 'Any amount from $0 to $2 is possible', 'sponsoring a child costs $1 a day or $30 a month'.
criteria.source_inquiry: Asks if the persuadee is familiar with or has heard of Save the Children.
criteria.task_inquiry: Asks the persuadee about giving, charities or the cause: 'Do you give to charity?', 'Do you care about this issue?', 'Have you heard about kids separated at the border?', 'Have you ever seen the rate of illiteracy?', 'Can I tell you anything more?'. Includes asking whether they know of or have seen a problem, when no figure is given.
criteria.personal_inquiry: Asks about the persuadee's own life: 'Are you a parent?', 'Where do you live?', 'What's your job?'.
